entries.proposition: Prior-work premise carried by the paper: Csnk1a1 haploinsufficiency activates Wnt and raises Myc in haematopoietic stem cells (citing earlier work, not shown here).
entries.snippet: Our previous work demonstrated that Csnk1a1 haploinsufficiency leads to a proliferative advantage of HSCs by activation of Wnt signaling and Myc upregulation

entries.proposition: The paper reports Wnt as up in leukaemic blasts by pathway-footprint inference and points to Figure 1 for the same in Csnk1a1-haploinsufficient cells.
entries.snippet: Pathway footprint analysis predicted downregulation of p53 pathways, as expected, and NF-κb and hypoxia pathways, whereas MAPK and Wnt signaling were upregulated (Figure 6C-D), as also seen in Csnk1a1 haploinsufficient hematopoietic stem cells (compare Figure 1).
entries.anchor: Results / Leukemic growth is driven by Wnt and Myc signaling

entries.proposition: Myc protein is claimed up only in the double-hit blasts, not in Csnk1a1 haploinsufficiency alone (a leukaemia-specific change).
entries.snippet: Myc induction was only observed in the Csnk1a1/Trp53 mutant blasts but not in Csnk1a1 haploinsufficiency or WT cells alone, indicating that Myc induction is leukemia specific.

entries.proposition: The text states that vehicle-treated leukaemias showed strong Myc induction and that A51 significantly reduced it (Fig 6I; mouse leukaemia, 5 mg/kg/day regimen, no neural tissue). The panel is one unquantified blot (6 untreated and 10 A51 lanes) with no statistic in the figure, legend or Methods, and Myc follows blast percentage (entry 21), so the reduction by A51 is stated, not demonstrated.
entries.snippet: Interestingly, vehicle-treated leukemias showed a strong induction of Myc, whereas A51 treatment significantly reduced the expression (Figure 6I).

contradicts_locator.what_changed: Auditor: quote is the text claim "significantly reduced", but Fig 6I is a single unquantified blot with no statistic and a blast-percentage confound. Proposition now says the effect is stated, not demonstrated.

audit.note: repair unaudited: the author of the repair does not certify it

entries.proposition: The collaborative transformation rests on one animal.
entries.snippet: Leukemia with blast dissemination and splenomegaly developed in the blood of 1 Csnk1a1–/+ Trp53 mouse (Figure 2C-E).
entries.anchor: Results / Collaborative effect of Trp53 mutations

entries.proposition: Selectivity of A51 for the double-hit blasts is stated for the higher dose of the A51 range.
entries.snippet: However, direct Csnk1a1 and Cdk7/9 inhibition with compound A51 notably caused growth arrest selectively in Trp53 mutant blasts at higher dose (Figure 4G).
entries.anchor: Results / Leukemic blasts can be cultured ex vivo

entries.proposition: The CK1 inhibitor D4476 was not significantly more efficient in Csnk1a1-/+ Hoxb8-Flt3 cells and blasts than in WT Hoxb8-Flt3 cells (in vitro, one drug). The source does not use this to say where within A51 the selective effect sits; no inference about a CK1-alpha versus CDK7/9 attribution is drawn from this comparison.
entries.snippet: Direct Csnk1a1 inhibition using D4476 was not significantly more efficient in Csnk1a1–/+ Hoxb8-Flt3 cells and blasts than in WT Hoxb8-Flt3 cells.

entries.proposition: In vitro screen: compounds and DMSO controls added in duplicate wells, cells cultured 24 hours, then an MTT proliferation assay. (The A51 concentration range shown in Fig 4G is attested in entry 19, not here.)
entries.snippet: The different compounds and their DMSO controls were added to the wells in duplicate in their own medium. Blasts in α-MEM (Hyclone) containing 10% FBS (Capricorn), 1% P/S (Sigma-Aldrich), Flt-3 (5ng/mL, Peprotech) and IL-7 (3ng/mL, Peprotech). HoxB8-Flt3 cells in IMDM (Gibco) containing 10% FBS (Capricorn), 1% P/S (Sigma-Aldrich), Flt-3 (40ng/mL, Peprotech) and B-estradiol (1μM Sigma-Aldrich). The cells were cultured for 24 hours after which the proliferation was measured according to protocol of the MTT Cell Growth Assay Kit
